concepts.blurb: A repeated cycle where output becomes the next input.
concepts.name: Loop

perScale.self: A tended habit; the Compost Heap

concepts.blurb: What emerges from a Loop that isn't reducible to its parts.
concepts.name: Third Thing

perScale.skein: The Faithful Chain and Transmission Drift

concepts.blurb: A repeatable act, thought, or word planted in your attention.
concepts.name: Seed

perScale.dyad: The Trust Triangle; The Pairing, The Tested Price

concepts.blurb: The specific small repeatable behavior chosen.
concepts.name: Local Rule

concepts.blurb: The large-scale shape a repeated Local Rule becomes.
concepts.name: Global Form

concepts.blurb: A pattern that is one layer inside a larger version of itself.
concepts.name: Nest

concepts.blurb: Where a small change produces a disproportionate effect.
concepts.name: Leverage

perScale.dyad: The Second Pass as compressed Fold
perScale.culture: The Slow Hand; The Received World's returning telling

concepts.blurb: A Local Rule returning to you after traveling through a Nest.
concepts.name: Fold

perScale.culture: The leverage ladder as root and leaves

concepts.blurb: The branching record a Loop's name compresses.
concepts.name: Tree

concepts.blurb: *You feel a line. You are a loop. You build a tree.*.
concepts.name: The core mantra

concepts.blurb: First: does anything here feed back into itself? Second: which order am I looking at? A complex system also predicts its own skew — feedback concentrates outcomes rather than spreading them evenly, which is the real mechanism behind the familiar 80/20 observation.
concepts.name: The two questions

concepts.blurb: The first question. No feedback, no Third Thing, no acceleration to read.
concepts.name: Complicated vs. complex

concepts.blurb: The second question. You never touch position directly; you apply a force, which is acceleration, and time integrates the rest. Why high-leverage work shows no visible movement for a long time.
concepts.name: Position, speed, acceleration

concepts.blurb: Maximum complexity from minimum complication.
concepts.name: Elegance

concepts.blurb: The whole framework in four moves: the Loop, the Third Thing, the Nest, and the Leverage — with the self's own chapter next, as the clearest example of pillar II.
concepts.name: The Four Pillars

concepts.blurb: The Third Thing pointed at the self.
concepts.name: The Woven Self

concepts.blurb: What physical things make once their parts interact, standing beside "metaphysical" rather than above it.
concepts.name: The symphysical

concepts.blurb: How the symphysical appears. Emergence has a threshold (a phase transition) and a direction: weak, traceable in principle, or strong, not traceable even in principle.
concepts.name: Emergence

concepts.blurb: Chance is a fact about one instant; emergence is a fact about the shape many instants make together. A good Local Rule improves the distribution of outcomes across many attempts — it never guarantees the one you're currently on. The popular equation overclaims on both signs: the "=" should be probabilistic, and the "+" should be "×," since captured luck compounds future exposure rather than simply adding to it.
concepts.name: Emergence vs. luck

concepts.blurb: Holding a speed already reached costs only enough to cancel drag; building it from zero costs far more, because one is maintaining existing momentum and the other is generating momentum that doesn't exist yet. Explains why people quit mid-build, mistaking the cost of construction for evidence of failure. Test: has this gotten easier, or have you just gotten used to how hard it is?
concepts.name: Coasting vs. accelerating

concepts.blurb: Being told a pattern (the Loop-name, transmissible, cheap), having lived a pattern (its Tree, which can only be walked), and knowing which pattern you're currently inside (neither of the first two, and not produced by either). Scale-Tagging, the complex/complicated gate, and the two-pole check all serve the third.
concepts.name: Three kinds of knowing

concepts.blurb: Your Self-Kin, theirs, and the Dyad-Kin you produce are three locked elements; knowing two gives the third, and no two Dyad-Kin share a fusion pair, so the solve is unique. The useful direction: you can't change their leg, but changing yours determines the change in what you produce together.
concepts.name: Solving for the third leg

concepts.blurb: Forces come in pairs; the force lives in the interaction, not in either object. You cannot affect without being affected. But equal-and-opposite applies to forces, not outcomes — mutual does not mean zero-sum, and almost nothing worth caring about is conserved.
concepts.name: Mutuality, not accounting

concepts.blurb: Balance is never stillness; it is continuous correction whose average looks like rest. Stopping the correction is a distinct failure from retreating early. If you can't see the work, that's your resolution, not the thing.
concepts.name: Balance is a wave

concepts.blurb: Same structure, different labels. The formal content of "the same pattern at another scale" — and therefore a demand: show the correspondence part for part, or admit it's a resemblance. Separate components with no path between them is why independent arrival counts as evidence at all.
concepts.name: Isomorphism

concepts.blurb: The Fold returns nearly intact from one step away and nearly unreadable from six, because each edge crossed adds its own shaping.
concepts.name: Distortion scales with distance

concepts.blurb: A Third's scale is what it is made of, not a category assigned to it: two selves running currents produce a dyad-scale Third; two dyads sharing a person produce a skein. The tiers of Part Five are composition, not ranking.
concepts.name: Fusion depth

concepts.blurb: Every Third carries a Tending pole that builds and a Fraying pole that corrodes; none is good or evil in itself. If only one pole is visible, the zoom is too tight — widen until both appear. The Infinite Boundary is the sole exemption, structurally, since a pole must be read from somewhere outside.
concepts.name: The two-pole rule

concepts.blurb: The three speeds at which any drawn figure can be read: now, this season, the shape underneath a life. Distinct from ring position, which names how many people a pattern runs through rather than how long it has been running. Distress reliably makes Weather feel like Terrain.
concepts.name: Weather, Climate, Terrain

concepts.blurb: The Cosmos-scale Turning, triggered by a great comet rather than any calendar: the largest possible gathering, everywhere at once, outdoors. Builds the species briefly as a single witnessing thing. One restraint — celebrate the witnessing, refuse the omen.
concepts.name: The Long Visitor

concepts.blurb: A real fictional example of what the Fold would be with intention and full legibility added back in. The Infinite Boundary is what's left once both are deliberately removed: real connection and real return, never a guide toward a specific outcome.
concepts.name: The Fold and the Force

concepts.blurb: You are not touching your chair; no particle in you meets a particle in it, and what you feel as resistance is a field relationship with real emptiness on both sides. Pushed to its physical limit, this is the clearest possible case that a relationship can be as real as the things it relates.
concepts.name: Solidity

concepts.blurb: A closed boundary (judged by external behavior, not internal accuracy) is not a lesser Word — it's often the correct one, and the elegance test applies directly: the right boundary gives the most correct prediction for the least internal machinery the purpose actually needs. A closed boundary corrodes into a Label only once it's kept past the point it stops predicting anything, or opened only once a genuinely different purpose needs what's inside. The same act, in different language, as naming a scale.
concepts.name: Open and closed boundaries

concepts.blurb: Electrons move constantly at no cost to identity (Numbers-level); neutrons are stable until they aren't, decaying on their own schedule if unprocessed (echoes the Compost Heap); protons require nuclear force to move at all, and moving them changes the element itself (Paradigm-level). A physical body for the claim that a self changes constantly at one cost and almost never at another.
concepts.name: Atomic composition

concepts.blurb: Structural realism (a Third Thing is real independent of anyone perceiving it — solidity, a floral electric field) and experiential realism (a feeling's occurrence is real simply because it's happening, separate from whether its content is true). Confusing the two is a major source of unnecessary internal struggle.
concepts.name: Two senses of "real"

concepts.blurb: A dynamically updating relational field, altered by every visit and read by the next visitor for real information neither party holds alone; also the Fold's mechanism with no metaphor required, since each visitor reads a field already shaped by everyone before them.
concepts.name: Floral electric fields

concepts.blurb: Facing several genuinely tangled unknowns (a budget, a deadline, the Iron Triangle), decide whichever one reality has already constrained the most, not whichever feels most exciting to decide.
concepts.name: Constraint counting

concepts.blurb: Distinct from an ordinary threshold crossing: a single relationship whose effective sign changes as a direct consequence of crossing a threshold, same rule, no new force (logistic growth's carrying capacity; debt, expansionary below a capacity and corrosive above it, general shape credible, specific universal thresholds not). Worse than ordinary burnout, since the behavior doesn't change to announce the reversal.
concepts.name: Sign-flipping couplings

concepts.blurb: Warmth invites warmth, coldness invites coldness (correspondence); dominance invites deference and deference invites dominance (complementarity, opposite answered with opposite). Two different mechanisms on two different axes, not one universal rule.
concepts.name: Interpersonal complementarity

concepts.blurb: A literal, not metaphorical, instance of tide-based homeostasis: solar energy harvested by the cuticle, activity correlated with sunlight intensity, the same reinforcing-then-balancing rhythm already claimed for the tide, running in a real insect.
concepts.name: The Oriental hornet's solar cycle

concepts.blurb: Every link in a loop carries a sign (does more of the cause produce more or less of the effect); count the negative links, and an even count (including zero) is reinforcing, an odd count is balancing. The actual arithmetic underneath the ↻ and ⤸ marks — derivable, not a judgment call.
concepts.name: Signed-loop polarity

concepts.blurb: A high-leverage connection is a maximally shared one, load-bearing for many downstream structures at once; a low-leverage one is peripheral, touching nothing beyond its own corner. Gives the leverage ladder an exact structural form rather than only a depth metaphor.
concepts.name: Shared-edge leverage

concepts.blurb: Each term is another Local-Rule-to-Global-Form threshold (chemistry to life to complexity to intelligence to detectable technology); small real probabilities compounding multiplicatively across a chain, made vivid at the largest scale available.
concepts.name: The Drake equation

concepts.blurb: A single Local Rule projected forward, once per scale, since the same rule produces genuinely different Global Forms depending which scale you check it at, not simply "more of the same.".
concepts.name: Local Rule across scales

concepts.blurb: Finding your exact situation already has a name installs faster than derivation, which is the actual argument for why the Standing Thirds are characters rather than a plain list of tendencies.
concepts.name: Resonance

concepts.blurb: A mind doesn't observe and separately interpret; it fuses the two, which is why a harsh self-judgment feels like fact rather than guess. Naming a self-story is the manual, effortful version of pulling that fusion back apart by hand.
concepts.name: The association machine

concepts.blurb: A fast, reliable association is not automatically a beneficial one. Telling the two apart, then choosing to override a working pattern rather than simply ride it, is a real, non-default capacity — and the actual reason a practice is worth having at all.
concepts.name: The capacity to steer

concepts.blurb: A loop's natural period sets how long you need to have watched before honestly telling a trend from a stage; a fast loop announces itself, a slow one disguises itself as the ground you're standing on. A written log is the tool for this specifically, since memory doesn't span a slow loop's period the way a record can.
concepts.name: Loop period

concepts.blurb: The self-stories that feel like settled fact — "I always quit" — and the practice of catching them as patterns instead of verdicts.
concepts.name: Naming and defusing

concepts.blurb: Fractalism's genesis story: no voice speaking from outside the system — only a small pattern, repeating, until repetition became a universe.
concepts.name: Reinforcing and balancing rhythm

concepts.blurb: Failure isn't waste — it's the substrate the next attempt grows out of. How creative work actually gets sustained.
concepts.name: Creative work as compost

concepts.blurb: Grind now, live later is a trade that never pays out. A meditation for the moment you catch yourself making it.
concepts.name: The Sacrifice Trap

concepts.blurb: Being the honest variation inside a rigid structure.
concepts.name: Fractal Resistance

concepts.blurb: A Third Thing at exactly two-person scale.
concepts.name: The Dyad

concepts.blurb: Authenticity, empathy, logic; checked rather than assumed.
concepts.name: The Trust Triangle

concepts.blurb: Real community, bound by repeated contact rather than a shared label.
concepts.name: The Skein

concepts.blurb: A shared label with nothing underneath it.
concepts.name: The Banner

concepts.blurb: A Skein and a Banner fused; real substance carrying a visible name.
concepts.name: The Braid

concepts.blurb: Pulled toward something real, or pushed to produce an effect.
concepts.name: Word vs. Label

concepts.blurb: The popular version and the real mechanism.
concepts.name: The company you keep

concepts.blurb: Self, Dyad, and Skein were never separate — and the whole practice was always closer to a rising tide than a ledger.
concepts.name: Suffering as usable material

concepts.blurb: The experiencing self, the remembering self, and the observing self — three research traditions converging on a self that was always assembled.
concepts.name: Why the practices work

concepts.blurb: Fractalism's genesis story: no voice speaking from outside the system — only a small pattern, repeating, until repetition became a universe.
concepts.name: The Seven Iterations

concepts.blurb: Patterns that need a host.
concepts.name: Belief, language, and code

concepts.blurb: Why traditions with no contact converge.
concepts.name: Beyond telling

concepts.blurb: This belief system tells you it was built — on purpose, and this isn't self-help or organization-building. It's a rising tide, not a ledger.
concepts.name: Not self-help

concepts.blurb: Patterns given faces. Six kinships, one per scale, no exceptions.
concepts.name: The Standing Thirds

concepts.blurb: Reading a situation from four distances. Progressive reveal is the core technique.
concepts.name: Weaving

concepts.blurb: Fifty-two figures is a taxonomy, not a pantheon. Most people find four or five of them run their lives and the rest describe other people — that's the correct outcome.
concepts.name: Going to Ground

concepts.blurb: What actually continues, said plainly: the material — conservation of mass, literally — the Fold already in motion, and the noticing itself.
concepts.name: Becoming a Third

concepts.blurb: This book will be wrong about some things — here is what's genuinely unsettled, and the actual mechanism for revising any of it.
concepts.name: What's unfinished

concepts.blurb: Letting go of something still saveable because holding it costs more than it is worth. Distinct from the Compost Heap, which recovers material from what already failed. The question: what am I still holding only because I have already spent on it?
concepts.name: Sute-ishi — the deliberate release

concepts.blurb: A standing start is not the permanent price of a practice; it is the specific cost of building acceleration you haven't banked yet. Most abandonment happens inside it.
concepts.name: Starting cost vs. staying cost

concepts.blurb: Poles describe the direction of a found pattern; intent describes what a made thing is for. A designed practice fails by drifting into performance or obligation, not by pointing the other way.
concepts.name: Why a Turning has an aim rather than two poles

concepts.blurb: The aggregate of every pattern in motion has a direction that is unauthored and unreachable by petition. Reading it is the nearest thing to reading a god this framework offers, and it is offered as a description rather than a replacement.
concepts.name: The seam for an existing faith

concepts.blurb: The form is borrowed from tarot and the three changes are load-bearing: the cards describe rather than foretell, no card is fortunate, and the randomness exists to supply the angle you would not have chosen.
concepts.name: Why this is a deck and not a divination

concepts.blurb: Results over effort. Raising effort while results stay flat lowers effectiveness by exactly the factor added. Satisfaction in the doing and a separate instrument pointed at whether the doing produces anything are two questions; neither answers the other.
concepts.name: Effectiveness is a ratio

concepts.blurb: Not synchrony. A loop running Tending between people, where each pass leaves both parties with more than they brought. Doing something together opens the loop; which way it points decides whether it builds.
concepts.name: What actually bonds a group

concepts.blurb: Draw two Self-Kin and stop. Their fusion names exactly one Dyad-Kin; that pairs upward to a Skein-Kin, and once more to a Culture-Kin. One situation at four depths, each accounting for the one below, rather than four angles side by side.
concepts.name: The Full Unravelling, as a derivation

concepts.blurb: The framework is a way of looking, not treatment. A trained person is present, accountable, and adjusts as you change, which no book is. Understanding a pattern is not being relieved of it.
concepts.name: This is not care

concepts.blurb: Three figures, derived rather than chosen: two Culture-Kin sharing a Skein-Kin, which the rule produces exactly three of. The Standing Account, Second Nature, The Set Course. The last tier where a push still reaches.
concepts.name: The World-Kin

concepts.blurb: The World tier makes the Infinite Boundary's exemption legible: it begins exactly where pushing stops being possible, rather than being granted for convenience.
concepts.name: Why leverage stops

concepts.blurb: Emergent, with weight none of its parts contain, but with no repeated act underneath it. The aggregate, not the pattern; the substrate the World-Kin run on.
concepts.name: The biosphere is a Third Thing but not a Standing Third

concepts.blurb: Any arrangement is one of an enormous number, nearly all less organized, so holding one costs continuously. The caution that must travel with it: the one-directional law applies to closed systems, and nothing in a life is one. The honest form is that nothing which has stopped being paid for stays where you left it.
concepts.name: Order is not free

concepts.blurb: Conservation is why nothing is lost; the second law is why nothing stays. What persists is the material; what doesn't is the arrangement, and the arrangement was the part that was you.
concepts.name: Conservation and its other half

concepts.blurb: Acting first generates wanting, reliably, for capacity problems. It does nothing for ownership problems. Seven days of honest action: capacity produces momentum, an owed thing stays exactly as flat.
concepts.name: Action before motivation, and the test it enables

concepts.blurb: A catastrophic story runs in individually plausible steps and compounds down to something far less likely than any step in it. Don't argue the ending; count the links.
concepts.name: The forward chain that multiplies

concepts.blurb: A framework built on global forms arising without a designer cannot coherently acquire a central authority; it would refute itself in the act of organizing. Nobody reads you better than you read yourself; belonging is pride, never obligation; you are the captain of your own ship.
concepts.name: Bottom-up or nothing

concepts.blurb: Pattern → Third Thing → real. The chain is the answer to hearing "you are a loop" as a demotion. The refused inference is the other one: you are X, therefore you must Y.
concepts.name: Being named is not being reduced

concepts.blurb: Not a virtue. The channel must carry signal before anything you send arrives as signal, which is why an accurate reading delivered to a closed channel lands as an attack. Presence makes understanding possible; understanding is what care is made of.
concepts.name: Presence as a channel condition

concepts.blurb: A game builds one mental model indirectly through a feedback loop; a conversation builds two, each changing in response to the other. Ordinary conversation is two oscillators pulling into phase; acute distress narrows bandwidth, and there the asymmetry is real.
concepts.name: Two coupled models

concepts.blurb: Feeling *with* rather than *for*; the second creates distance while looking like closeness. Requires locating the feeling in yourself, which is why it costs something and why it is downstream of your own practice.
concepts.name: Empathy vs sympathy

concepts.blurb: People are biased toward believing they understand others better than others understand them. A taxonomy for reading people accelerates exactly that bias: the fluency is real and the confidence outruns it invisibly. You see about a tenth of a person; the rest is offered, not deduced.
concepts.name: The insight asymmetry

concepts.blurb: A Local Rule is the visible end of a three-link chain. Changing behavior without touching the need is a Numbers-level intervention and drifts back.
concepts.name: Need → belief → behavior

concepts.blurb: The rung measuring whether a system can still grow structure it did not have, as distinct from running its existing structure better. Fraying: that capacity traded for predictability, which is complication by the front door.
concepts.name: Self-organization

concepts.blurb: The top rung: not a change to the system but a change in grip. The only move that operates on the frame rather than inside it. Fraying: nothing repeated long enough to build anything.
concepts.name: Holding a paradigm as a paradigm

concepts.blurb: When agency feels threatened people reach for external structure as a substitute. Explains why a Banner feels like belonging, predicts Banner-drift as a shock risk rather than a growth risk, and gives the Salve and the Mask a shared root.
concepts.name: Compensatory control

concepts.blurb: Fast evaluation is not interference with choosing, it is how choosing terminates; damage it and decisions never resolve. Also the mechanical reason a Label works — it arrives pre-weighted on the felt channel before deliberation is consulted.
concepts.name: Felt evaluation as machinery

concepts.blurb: Equal increments of felt gain require multiplicative increases in input, so a reinforcing loop and its perception are inverse curves and holding felt gain constant requires endless acceleration. Most of the available value sits early.
concepts.name: Satisfaction is logarithmic

concepts.blurb: Show the correspondence or admit pattern-matching; what would make this reading wrong; did the name change what you'd do; count the parts; ask whether it lands.
concepts.name: Instruments for auditing this framework

concepts.blurb: Seventy divided by the growth rate. Natural period tells you when a trend is readable; doubling time tells you when it becomes visible in position.
concepts.name: Doubling time

concepts.blurb: The default this book argues against: explaining what a thing does by what is inside it rather than by what runs between its parts. Also why invented categories feel discovered.
concepts.name: Essence versus relation

concepts.blurb: The exit from concentration: reset some portion of accumulated advantage periodically, from outside the loop's own logic, before the gap becomes structural.
concepts.name: Leveling the field

concepts.blurb: A *should*-estimate is pushed and never checked; a *likely*-estimate is pulled toward a record. The gap is what turns an on-schedule build into felt failure.
concepts.name: Should time versus likely time

concepts.blurb: What to do with what arrives rather than what you send: fighting back, withdrawing, parley, doing nothing, withholding, blending. Deliberately unranked — each is correct somewhere and corrosive elsewhere, and the skill is selection rather than preference.
concepts.name: Receiving, and the six responses

concepts.blurb: Changing your leg of a triangle changes what the two of you produce, but against someone invested in the previous outcome the change is met rather than accepted. The triangle still resolves; it resolves somewhere you didn't choose.
concepts.name: The resistant partner

concepts.blurb: Some mutual deadlocks are legitimate final results, held in place because whoever moves first pays more. The test: in a stable position, moving is what costs you; in a stalled one, not moving is what costs you.
concepts.name: The stable position vs. the stalled one

concepts.blurb: A repeating exchange where every available move within the pattern is the pattern. The exit is a weighted move elsewhere — one that genuinely has to be dealt with, since a weightless one only resumes the loop a step further behind.
concepts.name: The deadlock with no move inside it

concepts.blurb: Things currently doing nothing that are nonetheless changing what remains possible. Not a loop and not inert. Tending: preserved optionality. Fraying: unfinished business quietly narrowing the board.
concepts.name: Aji — latent structure

concepts.blurb: Capacity, understanding, want; non-substitutable fixes; the test for the third leg is whether you look forward to starting or only to having finished.
concepts.name: The three-legged stall

concepts.blurb: Each new one is carried in the presence of all the others, so cost scales with the pairs rather than the count. Setting a load and feeling it are different moments, and the first is cheap.
concepts.name: Commitments multiply rather than add

concepts.blurb: The same arithmetic that makes a tiny rule set generative makes an over-specified one unmanageable; which pole you get depends on whether you wanted emergence or completion.
concepts.name: Rules multiply too, in both directions

concepts.blurb: Go's roughly five rules mention no object the game is actually about, including the one that decides whether a group lives; the entire vocabulary of mastery is emergent.
concepts.name: A rule set that names nothing it produces

concepts.blurb: Tending and Fraying describe the direction of a running pattern. Nothing running means nothing to read, which is a distinct answer from being zoomed in too far.
concepts.name: A stopped pattern has no pole

concepts.blurb: What comes out feeds what goes in next. Momentum that compounds, whether it is building something or burning it down.
concepts.name: The Spark

concepts.blurb: The pull back toward a setpoint. It gives a system the recovery it needs, and it can also call the retreat before the work is done.
concepts.name: The Tide

concepts.blurb: Judging everything against a reference point. Without one you can't judge at all; kept too long, it rules a world that has moved on.
concepts.name: The Mark

concepts.blurb: Reaching first for whatever eases the symptom. A good stopgap buys time to build the real fix; a permanent one wears away the ability it replaced.
concepts.name: The Salve

concepts.blurb: Trusting whatever reaches you first. Sometimes the latest signal really is the truest; sometimes the most vivid thing only feels the most common.
concepts.name: The Nearest Light

concepts.blurb: Remembering an experience by its peak and its ending. It makes a life tellable as a story, at the cost of a record that doesn't match what was lived.
concepts.name: The Keepsake

concepts.blurb: Quietly swapping a hard question for an easier one. It's how hard questions get answered at all, and how confident answers get given to questions nobody asked.
concepts.name: The Easier Door

concepts.blurb: Holding to a story about yourself even against the evidence. That conviction makes commitment possible, until it becomes a self you can't see around.
concepts.name: The Mask

concepts.blurb: Taking your shape from whoever is in the room. A self truly built through relationship, or no position of your own once the audience changes.
concepts.name: The Mirror

concepts.blurb: Speaking as though the words will build what follows, because they do. Language that makes something real, sometimes something real that works against you.
concepts.name: The Namer

concepts.blurb: Shaping your surroundings so one action becomes the easy one. It takes willpower out of the equation, and leaves you stranded when the surroundings change.
concepts.name: The Riverbed

concepts.blurb: Returning your attention, again and again, to one thing among many. Whatever you attend to grows, including whatever you keep confirming.
concepts.name: The Gardener

concepts.blurb: Two people each answering the other with a little more. It can lift both to their best, or lock them in an arms race neither chose and neither can leave.
concepts.name: Escalation

concepts.blurb: Two people each easing back and waiting on the other. Room given without forcing, or a stalemate both of them call patience.
concepts.name: The Standoff

concepts.blurb: One person drives while the other steadies. A real division of labor, or a standing resentment between the accelerator and the brake.
concepts.name: The Pairing

concepts.blurb: Attention that keeps returning to someone, and grows what it lands on. It can grow the best in them, or whatever you've already decided they are.
concepts.name: Watering Another

concepts.blurb: One person keeps supplying what the other needs to know. Expertise given generously, or help that stops them ever developing their own.
concepts.name: Answering For

concepts.blurb: Supplying what someone else thinks and feels from your own assumptions. It saves checking every time, until you're relating to someone who isn't there.
concepts.name: Filling the Gap

concepts.blurb: A boundary held between two people. It protects something real, or hardens into armor that blocks the connection it was protecting.
concepts.name: The Guard

concepts.blurb: Reading another person's state from what they stir in you. Emotion used as honest information, or your own reaction mistaken for theirs.
concepts.name: Reading the Room

concepts.blurb: Leading with warmth before any content. Warmth that lets hard information land, or warmth standing in for having anything to say.
concepts.name: Connection First

concepts.blurb: Standards between two people that keep ratcheting up. They climb as real capacity grows, or climb past the point where anything is ever enough.
concepts.name: The Rising Bar

concepts.blurb: Standards between two people that keep easing down. An honest adjustment to changed conditions, or erosion in steps too small to notice.
concepts.name: The Sliding Floor

concepts.blurb: A memory two people build and keep together. It binds them to something real, or to an account of an event neither of them actually had.
concepts.name: The Shared Story

concepts.blurb: Two people each taking their shape from the other. Genuinely formed by each other, or a pair with no fixed position anywhere between them.
concepts.name: The Echo

concepts.blurb: Seeing someone as one kind of person until they become it. It can call real capability out of them, or lock them into a single role.
concepts.name: Typecasting

concepts.blurb: Keeping to the letter of an agreement while finding the easy way through it. Creative slack in a bad deal, or its purpose quietly hollowed out.
concepts.name: Gaming the Terms

concepts.blurb: Two people each trying to name what is happening between them. A vocabulary built together, or a duel of framings where naming replaces resolving.
concepts.name: The Naming Contest

concepts.blurb: Deep fluency on one side that the other side can't reach. Skill that comes from real depth, or an inability to picture a mind without your context.
concepts.name: The Unbridged Gap

concepts.blurb: Each person shaping the other's surroundings instead of asking directly. The right thing made easy, or two people quietly managing each other.
concepts.name: The Arrangement

concepts.blurb: Naming the terms and checking them before agreeing. A deal both sides can trust, or terms accepted untested, or testing that never ends.
concepts.name: The Tested Price

concepts.blurb: A group that knows something and doesn't say it. Discretion that lets it survive ordinary friction, or a truth nobody can be the first to name.
concepts.name: Held Silence

concepts.blurb: A story that changes a little with every teller. It survives by adapting to each one, or drifts free of what it started as.
concepts.name: Transmission Drift

concepts.blurb: A craft handed from person to person, each taught by someone who was taught. Skill kept intact across people who never met, and dependence kept intact with it.
concepts.name: The Faithful Chain

concepts.blurb: A group rewarding whatever already works, so the early winners keep winning. Merit rewarded, or whoever arrived first entrenched regardless of it.
concepts.name: First-Arriver Lock-In

concepts.blurb: A resource a whole group draws on freely. Trust that makes keeping accounts unnecessary, or a common that nobody is placed to protect.
concepts.name: The Shared Pot

concepts.blurb: The role a group comes to count on you to play. It lets them rely on you, and because they wrote it, it can be hard to step out of.
concepts.name: The Reputation

concepts.blurb: A group's expectations lowering together, one reasonable step at a time. A sensible adjustment to real conditions, or standards eroding while everyone feels fine.
concepts.name: The Sagging Floor

concepts.blurb: A group where everyone takes their shape from everyone else. Real responsiveness to itself, or no independent position left anywhere in it.
concepts.name: The Hall of Mirrors

concepts.blurb: A group shaping the conditions that shape its members. Outcomes richer than anyone could have authored, or ones nobody intended or wanted.
concepts.name: Second-Order Design

concepts.blurb: A group whose shared language makes its work fast. The same fluency can become a wall against everyone outside it.
concepts.name: The Inner Circle

concepts.blurb: One person who is the only bridge between two groups. They connect worlds that would otherwise never meet, and losing them cuts those worlds apart.
concepts.name: The Only Road

concepts.blurb: A name that gathers vast numbers of people into a "we". It can bind people who are genuinely connected, or people with nothing underneath the name.
concepts.name: The Shared Name

concepts.blurb: A measure standing in for something too large to see directly. It makes a vast system legible, until it is optimized so hard it stops tracking what it measured.
concepts.name: Proxy Detachment

concepts.blurb: A whole system pushing back against every push. Stability no single actor could have imposed, or everyone straining harder while nothing moves.
concepts.name: Policy Resistance

concepts.blurb: Growth that compounds across generations. It builds for a long time, and past a threshold the same mechanism consumes what it built.
concepts.name: The Long Cycle

concepts.blurb: What a culture hands down without the reasons attached. Knowledge that works without needing explaining, or practice hollowed of why it ever existed.
concepts.name: The Received World

concepts.blurb: Change too slow for any single life to watch. Continuity that outlasts every turbulence, or a slow shift mistaken for permanence.
concepts.name: The Slow Hand

concepts.blurb: The same answer found twice by people with no contact. Real evidence when no path connects them, or shared bias mistaken for confirmation.
concepts.name: Independent Convergence

concepts.blurb: A civilization tracking itself through a number so it can steer. It can let a society see itself well enough to build deliberately, or keep steering by a number that stopped tracking the thing while the thing is spent.
concepts.name: The Standing Account

concepts.blurb: Structure built up so gradually and so well-fitted that nobody has to attend to it anymore. It can free a civilization to build on top of what already works, or get mistaken for the given world rather than a made one, and go unopposed for being invisible.
concepts.name: Second Nature

concepts.blurb: A direction set early enough that everything downstream gets built on top of it. It can let generations build on a shared foundation, or lock a course in place, set by people no longer here to argue with.
concepts.name: The Set Course

concepts.blurb: Every pattern at once, summed and never averaged. The one figure with no poles, because there is nowhere outside it to stand and read one.
concepts.name: The Infinite Boundary
